name: Albinism-Deafness Syndrome

criteria.description: Pigmentary abnormalities of the hair, skin, or eyes including hypopigmentation or patches of depigmentation
Heterochromia iridis or brilliant blue irides
Presence of a white forelock or early graying of hair
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital sensorineural deafness and at least one major pigmentary abnormality
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; genetic testing for mutations in MITF or other related genes may support diagnosis.

laboratory: Audiometric testing confirming sensorineural hearing loss
Skin biopsy showing reduced melanin pigmentation
imaging: Temporal bone CT or MRI may show cochlear abnormalities
genetic: Mutations in SOX10 or SNAI2 genes in some cases
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of iris heterochromia and white forelock
Congenital white forelock and skin hypopigmentation without hearing loss
Generalized hypopigmentation with visual impairment but no hearing loss
Ocular findings such as nystagmus and foveal hypoplasia

redFlags: Early onset patchy hypopigmentation of skin and hair
Family history of similar pigmentary and auditory abnormalities
references: Read AP, Newton VE. Waardenburg syndrome. J Med Genet. 1997;34(8):656-65.
Tassabehji M. Waardenburg syndrome type 2 and MITF. Clin Genet. 2003;63(5):355-61.
Orphanet: Albinism-deafness syndrome. Orphanet Report Series. 2024.
